correctness.rationale: The exact phase-damping concurrence condition C_s>0 is equivalent to s|ad-bc|>(1-s^2)sqrt(|ad bc|). With four independent circular complex Gaussian coordinates before Haar normalization, the two squared product magnitudes are independent products of two exponentials. Their ratio has exact CDF F(h)=h log(1/h)/(1-h)^2-h/(1-h). On A<=B, triangle inequalities show t/(1+t^2)<=sqrt(AB)/|P-Q|<=t/(1-t^2), t=sqrt(A/B), implying a sharp phase-independent 2F(v_-^4)<=p(s)<=2F(v_+^4) for 0<s<sqrt(2)-1. Both ends expand to 8s^4 log(1/s)-2s^4+O(s^6 log(1/s)). Exact logarithmic and constant terms follow from the squeeze, not stochastic simulation. An independent partial-transpose eigensolver for 1600 Gaussian-Haar states at each s=0.1,0.35,0.7 found zero disagreements with the concurrence threshold (4800 checks).
residual_risks: Only complex-Haar pure initial states and identical independent local dephasing, with p(s) for s tending to zero.
